2.text: MIXTURE WITH OTHER TRIBES. — Notwithstanding considerable diversity

3.text: in the features of the Chukchee, I doubt whether their blood is much mixed.

4.text: At present the Reindeer men do not hesitate to take wives from among the

5.text: Russians, the Lamut, or the Chuvantzy; but these intermarriages are of recent

6.text: date. All cases of such intermarriages are on record, and they are but very

7.text: few in number. Moreover, the births resulting from the marriages of Russian

8.text: women (or, more strictly speaking, of Russianized Yukaghir women) with

9.text: Chukchee men have not been numerous. The reason for this is probably

10.text: that these women, who are not very prolific in their native environment, are

11.text: still less so under the conditions of nomad arctic life.

12.text: On the Koryak border considerable intermixing with this tribe is going

13.text: on at the present time. The Maritime Chukchee may have been intermixed

14.text: with the Eskimo from ancient times. At the present date, in the village of

21.text: FERTILITY. — The Chukchee are the healthiest of the tribes in north-

22.text: eastern Siberia. Their families contain more children than those of any of

23.text: their neighbors. While taking the census in the Kolyma district in 1897, I

24.text: came across sèveral families having five, seven, and even nine children living.
24.resolved: sèveral = s, e+U+0300 (combining grave accent), v, e, r, a, l
24.note: Printed 'several' carries a visible grave accent over the first e (confirmed at 4x, 24@8) — not a standard English orthographic feature, most likely a stray/damaged sort from setting. Reproduced as printed (è, e+U+0300) per the print-reproduction default for English prose; flagging for adjudication since this is not a catalogued English convention.

25.text: Ten per cent of the families had not less than five children living. One man

26.text: had by two wives twelve children living. Another, by seven wives (three of

27.text: them dead), had fourteen children living.

28.text: On the Pacific coast, among the Maritime Chukchee, one woman had

29.text: had thirteen children (seven living and six dead); another one, eleven (three

30.text: living and eight dead); still another, nine (five living and four dead); etc.

31.text: Several times, chiefly among the Reindeer Chukchee, I met with twins. This

32.text: degree of fertility results in the steady increase of the Chukchee, especially

33.text: among the Reindeer division, in spite of the contagious diseases which ravage

34.text: the country once every ten or fifteen years. It is interesting to note that

35.text: even among the Kamchadal, who are steadily decreasing in numbers, I came

36.text: across several women with many children. One, for instance, had eight living

37.text: and two dead; another, five living and ten dead; a third, five living, two

38.text: dead, and five abortions; a fourth, seven living, three dead, and three abortions;

39.text: a fifth, six living, two dead, and two abortions; etc.: so that here, at least,

40.text: the decrease is not produced by any reduction in the number of births.

41.text: As far as can be ascertained, the decrease of native tribes in northeastern

42.text: Siberia was produced by the direct or even indirect contact with civilization,
